correctness.rationale: Reconstructed matching complex X=Ind(line graph W_11). Rim-only subcomplex Ind(C_10)≃S^2; all spoke cones attach along copies of Ind(P_8)≃S^2, proving simply-connected X. Two D_10 generating reflections each fix an actual matching vertex (a fixed spoke and a fixed rim edge), so Armstrong orbit-fundamental-group theorem gives π1(X/D_10)=0. Independently generated all matchings of sizes one through five, counts [20,115,260,225,52], all barycentric chains and their D_10 orbits [43,343,882,894,312]. Constructed the exact oriented integral orbit-boundary matrices, checked boundary squared zero, and computed all four complete integer Smith forms with SymPy (not merely cited archived logs): ranks 42,301,581,312 and no nonunit invariant factors for any B_d. Hence H_0=H_3=Z with no torsion, all other reduced integral homology zero. Simply connected plus H2=0 gives 2-connected; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead then identify the full ordinary quotient as S^3. This is an exhaustive finite computation for the specified 20-edge graph.
residual_risks: The integral Smith normal-form computation uses a trusted exact integer algorithm; independent matrix assembly was separately implemented and checked against recorded ranks.
Armstrong requires the simply-connected covering space and fixed point stabilizers; these are verified for the ordinary topological action, not a free action.

value.rationale: For a canonical symmetry quotient of a natural graph matching complex, the known rational invariant H3=Q left integral torsion and π1 unknown. The exact quotient S3 homotopy classification resolves these genuinely non-implied topological invariants with a reproducible finite integer chain model. Nonfree actions make invariant homology insufficient; the result is a substantive integral upgrade for a symmetry-distinguished first example.
